### 2. file-snapshot-capture-helper-consolidation

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | The exists→`ReadAllBytes`/`FromExistingBytes` vs missing→fallback-text-or-null decision is inlined independently at 6 call sites across 4 files (confirmed live via `find_references` on `FileSnapshotDto.FromExistingBytes` — all 6 resolve; matches the row's cited anchors plus one extra found by the tool): `EditService.cs:82-89` (`ApplyTextEditsAsync`) — async self-read via `File.Exists`+`ReadAllBytesAsync`, fallback = already-parsed `sourceText`; `EditService.cs:143-151` (`ApplyMultiFileTextEditsAsync` loop) — same shape per batched file; `EditorConfigService.cs:353-357` (`SetOptionAsync`) — reuses a SYNC-read `existingBytes` local already captured at line 345 (also reused at line 380 for BOM/encoding detection); fallback = null; `ProjectMutationService.cs:557-562` (`ApplyProjectMutationAsync`) — reuses an ASYNC-read `preApplyBytes` local also reused at line 573 for `AtomicFileWriter.ResolveWriteEncoding(preApplyBytes)`; fallback = null; `RefactoringService.cs:1057-1089` (`AddFileSnapshotAsync`) — the most complete/general form (exists→bytes; missing+`missingFileIsNew`→null; missing+existing-document→`document.GetTextAsync()` text) — the exemplar the row's Evidence cites as already-correct. A 6th call site, `RefactoringService.cs:1091-1108` (`AddProjectFileSnapshotAsync`, found via `find_references`, not cited by the backlog row), early-returns on missing files with no fallback branch at all — it does not duplicate the 3-way policy and is out of scope. Root cause: no shared factory owns "given bytes-or-null, produce the right `FileSnapshotDto`", so each site hand-rolls its own ternary; two of them (`EditorConfigService`, `ProjectMutationService`) additionally re-derive/reuse the exists-check for a SECOND purpose (BOM/encoding detection), so the extracted helper must accept already-read bytes rather than performing its own I/O for those two, or they'd read the file twice. |
| Approach | Add `internal static class FileSnapshotCapture` in a new file `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/FileSnapshotCapture.cs`, mirroring the placement/style of `AtomicFileWriter` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompositeApplyOrchestrator.cs:140-179` — an `internal static class` colocated in `Services/`, XML-doc'd, `ConfigureAwait(false)` throughout). Two static members: (1) `internal static FileSnapshotDto FromBytesOrFallback(string filePath, byte[]? bytes, string? fallbackText)` — the pure, no-I/O policy (`bytes is not null ? FileSnapshotDto.FromExistingBytes(filePath, bytes) : new FileSnapshotDto(filePath, fallbackText)`); lets `EditorConfigService`/`ProjectMutationService` pass their ALREADY-READ `existingBytes`/`preApplyBytes` locals without a second disk read. (2) `internal static async Task<FileSnapshotDto> CaptureAsync(string filePath, string? fallbackText, CancellationToken ct)` — convenience for callers without pre-read bytes (`File.Exists` + `File.ReadAllBytesAsync` then delegates to `FromBytesOrFallback`); used by both `EditService.cs` sites. Call-site changes: `EditService.cs:82-89` → `await FileSnapshotCapture.CaptureAsync(normalizedFilePath, sourceText.ToString(), ct).ConfigureAwait(false)`; `EditService.cs:143-151` → same pattern per loop item using `t.SourceText.ToString()`; `EditorConfigService.cs:353-357` → `FileSnapshotCapture.FromBytesOrFallback(editorconfigPath, existingBytes, fallbackText: null)` (sync — no signature/async change needed to `SetOptionAsync`, which currently returns via `Task.FromResult` with no other awaits); `ProjectMutationService.cs:557-562` → keep the existing `preApplyBytes` read (still needed for `ResolveWriteEncoding` at line 573), replace only the ternary with `FileSnapshotCapture.FromBytesOrFallback(normalizedProjectFilePath, preApplyBytes, fallbackText: null)`. Deferred (explicit follow-up, NOT in this initiative's scope): `RefactoringService.cs:1057-1089` (`AddFileSnapshotAsync`) already implements the correct policy and is not at risk; converting it to delegate is a trivial 1-file follow-up once `FileSnapshotCapture` exists — scoped out here solely to keep this initiative within Rule 3's 4-production-file cap (helper + 3 call-site files = 4; adding `RefactoringService.cs` makes 5). |
| Scope | Production files (4, all within Rule 3's hard cap — no exemption claimed): NEW `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/FileSnapshotCapture.cs`; modified `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditService.cs` (2 call sites); modified `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditorConfigService.cs`; modified `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ProjectMutationService.cs`. `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/RefactoringService.cs` is deliberately excluded from this initiative's scope (see Approach/Backlog sync) — that is how the 5-site refactor fits the 4-file cap. No files deleted. |

### 3. core-dto-location-quartet-consolidation-primary

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `LocationDto` already exists (`src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/LocationDto.cs`: `FilePath, StartLine, StartColumn, EndLine, EndColumn, ContainingMember, PreviewText, Classification`), but `SymbolDto` (`src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/SymbolDto.cs:6-27`), `DiagnosticDto` (`src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/DiagnosticDto.cs:6-15`), and `TypeUsageDto` (`src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/TypeUsageDto.cs:34-42`) each re-declare their own flat `FilePath`/`StartLine`/`StartColumn`/`EndLine`/`EndColumn` fields instead of composing it - confirmed by direct read of all four files. Composing `LocationDto` into these public-response DTOs is a breaking wire-shape change (per `docs/release-policy.md`'s compatibility policy), and the item file's Evidence records direct removal spanning >=12 production files + 6 test files - too large for one initiative and gated on an operator decision. That decision was made 2026-08-06 (recorded in the item file's Decision section, resolved via `/defer-unblock`): additive nested `Location` field + legacy-flat-field deprecation window, NOT a major-version replacement; a prior `[JsonIgnore]`-only computed view was already rejected because external consumers couldn't adopt a non-serialized property. This initiative's own do-cell text (`"Write LocationDto migration ADR + plan ... Record the ADR, then split into bounded migration stages"`) scopes the deliverable to a durable ADR + migration plan artifact, not the DTO code change itself - the code change is deferred to a future bounded stage-1 row (filed at backlog-sync) plus the already-existing, still-blocked `core-dto-location-quartet-consolidation-secondary` row. No bundle peers were supplied (`bundleCandidatePeers: []`); Rule 1 is n/a. |
| Approach | Create `docs/decisions/0001-locationdto-nested-field-migration.md` (new `docs/decisions/` directory - no prior ADR convention exists in this repo; this establishes one) using a standard ADR shape (Status / Context / Decision / Consequences). Context cites the flat-field duplication at `SymbolDto.cs:6-27`, `DiagnosticDto.cs:6-15`, `TypeUsageDto.cs:34-42` vs. the existing `LocationDto.cs` shape. Decision restates the 2026-08-06 operator call verbatim (additive nested field, rejects `[JsonIgnore]`-only). Cover every Acceptance bullet as its own subsection: (1) wire shape - new optional `Location: LocationDto?` property added alongside the existing flat fields on `SymbolDto`/`DiagnosticDto`/`TypeUsageDto`, populated by producers `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/SymbolMapper.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/DiagnosticService.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompileCheckService.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/MutationAnalysisService.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/DotnetOutputParser.cs` (all five confirmed to exist) once stage 1 lands; (2) null/partial-location semantics - `Location` is null when a producer cannot resolve a span, mirroring the existing nullable-flat-field pattern; (3) legacy-flat deprecation window - cite `docs/release-policy.md`'s 'Deprecate stable entries for at least one minor release before removal'; flat fields get `[Obsolete]` one minor release after `Location` ships, removed at the next major; (4) semver - additive field is minor-version-safe per release-policy's 'Adding stable tools/resources/prompts is a minor-version change', extended here to DTO field additions; eventual flat-field removal is the major-version trigger; (5) record constructor compatibility - the new `Location` parameter must be appended with a default (`LocationDto? Location = null`) at the END of each record's positional-parameter list so existing positional `new SymbolDto(...)`/`new DiagnosticDto(...)`/`new TypeUsageDto(...)` call sites (source + test fixtures) keep compiling; (6) `with` expressions - unaffected, records support partial `with` updates on any property subset; (7) equality - record structural equality automatically includes the new property once populated, so downstream snapshot/equality comparisons will see `Location` join the compared surface - flag explicitly as a breaking-for-equality-consumers risk even under the 'additive' framing. (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompositeApplyOrchestrator.cs:82` — `ApplyCompositeAsync` calls `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync(mutation.FilePath, mutation.UpdatedContent ?? string.Empty, ct, _logger)` with no `encoding:` argument, so every composite-apply write silently re-encodes as UTF-8-no-BOM regardless of the file's original BOM/encoding — the same class of bug PR #1157 fixed in `EditService.PersistDocumentTextToDiskAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditService.cs:702-725`) and `ProjectMutationService.ApplyProjectMutationAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ProjectMutationService.cs:557-573`), just not applied to this third write path. ### 7. compile-check-zero-resolution-false-success

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompileCheckService.cs:300-322` (`ResolveProjectScope`) combined with `:199-213` (`ShouldReportDiagnostic`): when a `files` filter resolves to zero owning projects (`FindOwningProjects` returns an empty set → `owningProjects.Count==0` at line 316-319), `ResolveProjectScope` widens to the full project list (`filteredProjects`, effectively every loaded project since `projectFilter` is unset on this branch) instead of failing. `CheckAsync` (line 54) then runs `CollectDiagnosticsAsync` against every widened project, but `ShouldReportDiagnostic` still filters every returned diagnostic against the ORIGINAL non-matching `normalizedFileFilters` — since none of those requested paths exist in the workspace, every diagnostic (including genuine solution-wide compile errors) is dropped and `acc.ErrorCount` stays 0. `Success` (line 82) only guards `CompletedProjects > 0`, which the widened compile satisfies, so `compile_check` returns `Success:true, ErrorCount:0, CompletedProjects:N` against a solution that may be carrying thousands of real errors (witnessed: 18,274 CS errors in the PR #1160 repro cited in the row's Evidence). This is distinct from the existing `CompletedProjects==0` guard added for `compile-check-zero-projects-claimed-success-after-reload` (Item #6, regression-tested in `CompileCheckZeroProjectsTests.cs`) — that guard covers "nothing ran"; this row is the "everything ran, matched nothing, still reported green" arm, matching the row's own `## Context` note. No Rule 1 bundling applies — `bundleCandidatePeers` is empty. |
| Approach | Single-file, root-cause fix confined to three small edits in `CompileCheckService.cs`, all within the code already cited by the row's anchor: (1) In `ResolveProjectScope`, split the shared "reason" string builder so the `owningProjects.Count==0` arm returns an EMPTY project list (`([], hint)`) instead of falling back to `filteredProjects`. This is the smallest change that reuses the ALREADY-CORRECT `CompletedProjects > 0` precondition on `Success` (line 82) rather than adding a new field or a parallel Success computation — the empty list naturally drives `CompletedProjects==0`/`TotalProjects==0`, flipping `Success` to `false` and giving this case the exact contract Item #6 already established for "projectFilter matched nothing." The `owningProjects.Count > 1` ("resolved to multiple projects") arm is intentionally UNCHANGED — that fallback is legitimate (files genuinely span multiple projects, so widen-then-filter-by-path is the correct behavior) and is already regression-tested by `CheckAsync_FileFiltersAcrossProjects_FallsBackToFullScopeWithHint`. (2) In `BuildHint`, narrow the generic `zeroProjectsHint` guard from `!acc.Cancelled && projectCount == 0` to also require `fileScopeHint is null`, so the new zero-resolution-specific hint text is not obscured by the unrelated "workspace may have completed a reload" message when both would otherwise fire together (this combination never occurred before this fix, since the file-filter fallback previously always produced `projectCount > 0`). (3) In `CheckAsync`'s `actualScope` computation (line 75), tighten the ternary from `fileScopeHint is not null ? ScopeSolution : requestedScope` to also require `projectList.Count > 0`, so the zero-resolution case reports `ActualScope == RequestedScope == "files"` (nothing was actually widened or compiled) instead of the now-misleading `"solution"`. No DTO changes needed — `CompileCheckDto`/`CompileCheckOptions` already carry every field this fix needs (`Success`, `CompletedProjects`, `TotalProjects`, `RestoreHint`, `RequestedScope`, `ActualScope`). |

### 12. compile-check-restorehint-empty-not-null

Its `<summary>` (lines 234-240) claims the method returns `null` "when neither applies," but the terminal statement (line 270-271) is `return string.Join(" ", new[] { zeroProjectsHint, restoreHint, fileScopeHint }.Where(...));` — `string.Join` over a filtered-to-empty sequence returns `string.Empty`, never `null`, per BCL contract. The bug is self-documented: the adjacent comment at `CompileCheckService.cs:73` ("BuildHint joins into an empty string, never null, when no hint applies") was added in PR #1151 but only tracked as a comment, not fixed. `CompileCheckDto.RestoreHint` (`src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/CompileCheckDto.cs:41`) is `string?` with no `[JsonIgnore(Condition = WhenWritingNull)]`/`WhenWritingDefault`, so every clean `compile_check` response (no CS0234 flood, no zero-projects fallback, no file-filter widening) serializes `"restoreHint": ""` instead of omitting the field or emitting `null` — misleading callers who probe for hint presence. Test-side, `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/CompileCheckServiceTests.cs:61` (`Assert.IsNotNull(result.RestoreHint)`) is vacuous against this exact bug: an empty string also satisfies `IsNotNull`, so the assertion cannot catch the empty-vs-null discrepancy even though it sits in a test that (correctly) expects a *populated* hint. No test currently asserts the clean-response case is `null`. Confirmed `RestoreHint` on `CompileCheckDto` is unrelated to the like-named field on `WorkspaceStatusSummaryDto` (`src/RoslynMcp.Core/Models/WorkspaceStatusSummaryDto.cs:48`, consumed by `WorkspaceReadinessReportBuilder.cs`/`WorkspaceSupportBundleBuilder.cs`) — that DTO's own `BuildRestoreHint` already returns `null` correctly, so no cross-file blast radius. `bundleCandidatePeers` is empty — no Rule 1 bundling to evaluate. |
| Approach | Single-file fix in `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompileCheckService.cs`: change `BuildHint`'s final `return` to check the joined result before returning, e.g. `var joined = string.Join(" ", new[] { zeroProjectsHint, restoreHint, fileScopeHint }.Where(static h => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(h))); return string.IsNullOrEmpty(joined) ? null : joined;` — this makes the implementation match its own `<summary>` contract and removes the stale line-73 comment's need to exist (the comment becomes accurate by construction and can be trimmed). Test-side, in `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/CompileCheckServiceTests.cs`: (1) extend `CheckAsync_FileFilterOwnedByOneProject_CompilesOnlyOwningProject` (lines 16-42 — a clean, single-owning-project scoped check with zero errors) with `Assert.IsNull(result.RestoreHint, "A clean scoped compile check with no CS0234 flood, zero-projects fallback, or file-filter widening must not carry a restoreHint.");` — this is the Acceptance item 2's "test asserting restoreHint is null/absent on a clean scoped check," added to the existing clean-scope test rather than a new file (Rule 6 — smallest complete fix). (2) Replace the vacuous `Assert.IsNotNull(result.RestoreHint);` at line 61 with `Assert.IsFalse(string.IsNullOrEmpty(result.RestoreHint), "Fallback restoreHint must be non-empty when file filters span multiple projects.");` — an assertion that actually fails on the empty-string regression this row exists to prevent. | Diagnosis | `ValidationServiceOptions.GitStatusTimeout`'s XML doc (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ValidationServiceOptions.cs:48-56`) and the `ROSLYNMCP_GIT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` row in `ai_docs/runtime.md:63` both state the timeout "bounds only the `git status --porcelain` invocation that `validate_recent_git_changes` uses to derive its changed-file scope." That is incomplete: `_gitStatusTimeout` is passed to `CollectGitChangedFilesAsync` at TWO call sites in `WorkspaceValidationService.cs` — `ValidateRecentGitChangesAsync` (`WorkspaceValidationService.cs:137`) AND `ReconcileChangeTrackerFilesAsync` (`WorkspaceValidationService.cs:314`), the latter invoked from `validate_workspace`'s change-tracker fallback path (via `ValidateInternalAsync:222`) whenever the caller omits `changedFilePaths`. The two call sites behave differently on timeout: `ValidateRecentGitChangesAsync` degrades `OverallStatus` to `git-status-unknown` (see `DegradeStatusWhenGitStatusUnknown`, `WorkspaceValidationService.cs:192-197`); `ReconcileChangeTrackerFilesAsync` deliberately discards the `TimedOut` flag (comment at `:310-313`: "scoped to `ValidateRecentGitChangesAsync` only") and silently falls back to the unfiltered tracker list — no verdict degradation, no warning. The docs currently imply the knob only affects the first, narrower, degrading path; a repo/CI environment tuning `ROSLYNMCP_GIT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` for `validate_recent_git_changes` needs to know the same value also gates `validate_workspace`'s reconcile precision, silently, with different failure semantics. Audited the other `ValidationServiceOptions` timeout fields (`BuildTimeout`, `TestTimeout`, `VulnerabilityScanTimeout`, `ApplyRevertTimeout`) — none of their XML docs or `runtime.md` rows name a single call site that is actually one of several; only `GitStatusTimeout` carries the narrowed-scope defect, satisfying backlog acceptance criterion 2 as a completed audit (no further `runtime.md` row needs correction). |
| Approach | Doc-only correction, two files, no behavior change. (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ValidationServiceOptions.cs:47-55` — rewrite the `GitStatusTimeout` XML `<summary>` to state it bounds the `git status --porcelain` subprocess at both `WorkspaceValidationService.CollectGitChangedFilesAsync` call sites: the `validate_recent_git_changes` scope-collection path (which degrades `OverallStatus` to `git-status-unknown` on timeout) AND the `validate_workspace` change-tracker reconcile path in `ReconcileChangeTrackerFilesAsync` (which silently falls back to the unfiltered tracker list on timeout, no verdict change). (2) `ai_docs/runtime.md:63` — extend the `ROSLYNMCP_GIT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` row's "Affects" cell to name both call sites and the asymmetric on-timeout behavior, mirroring the corrected XML doc's wording so the two doc surfaces stay in sync (existing repo pattern: `runtime.md` env-var rows restate the bound `ValidationServiceOptions` field's XML doc in table form). No code, test, or DI changes — `_gitStatusTimeout` itself is untouched. |
| Scope | Production files (2): `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ValidationServiceOptions.cs` (XML doc comment only), `ai_docs/runtime.md` (table cell only). Test files (0) — pure documentation correction, no executable-behavior change, nothing to regression-test. No Rule-3 exemption needed (well under the 4-file cap). |
